title: Extract information from video · Level 3
slo: Describe the information a video analyzer can extract from a meeting.

exercises.question_text: What can downstream systems do with structured media results? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Structured results can be stored for later use.
This is correct. Structured results can be searched.
This is correct. Structured results can be passed to downstream automation.

options.error_type: Confuses extracted results with source media
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Structured results are extracted information and do not replace the original recording.
options.better_fit: Use this idea only when discussing a separate meeting record, not extracted results.

feedback.intrinsic: Important context from the original recording could be lost.
feedback.instructional: Use structured results to store, search, analyze, and automate information.

exercises.explanation: Correct—structured results can support storage, search, and automation.

exercises.question_text: The conference-room image returned three attendees in total.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: One attendee would be omitted from the meeting count.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Three is the remote count; one in-person attendee makes four total.

exercises.explanation: Correct—the total was four, not three.

exercises.question_text: What can video analysis extract from a recorded meeting?

options.rationale: This is correct. Video meeting analysis can extract attendance and assigned actions.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with document OCR
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Printed text is associated with OCR for documents and images, not the full range of meeting-video insights.
options.better_fit: Use this for a scanned page or receipt image when the goal is to read printed text.

feedback.intrinsic: The coordinator would miss attendance and follow-up actions.
feedback.instructional: Video analysis can capture meeting details beyond printed text.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with voicemail extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A callback number is a call-detail field and does not represent the range of meeting details available from video.
options.better_fit: Use this for a voicemail schema that extracts contact details.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting review would focus on one call detail.
feedback.instructional: Callback numbers fit calls; video can also provide attendance and actions.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with invoice extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Totals and tax are invoice fields, not meeting details extracted from video.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing an invoice for billing amounts.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting record would not identify attendees or actions.
feedback.instructional: Invoice fields belong to invoice analysis; video can capture meeting information.

exercises.explanation: Correct—video analysis can reveal attendance and assigned actions.

exercises.question_text: prebuilt-audioSearch is the prebuilt analyzer selected for video input.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A recorded video conference would be treated as the wrong media type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: For video input, select prebuilt-videoSearch rather than an audio analyzer.

exercises.explanation: Correct—an audio analyzer is not selected for video input.

exercises.question_text: The conference-room camera image identified the location as ___.

parts.text: The conference-room camera image identified the location as

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The location field would not describe the place shown by the camera.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Conference room is the returned location; a voicemail or recording is not a location.

exercises.explanation: Location is a defined field for the camera image. The returned location value is Conference room.

exercises.question_text: A meeting-services lead must select an analyzer for recorded video conferences and deliver structured meeting details to a reporting system. Which decisions best fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. It is the prebuilt analyzer selected for video input.
This is correct. The stated reporting need requires structured information from the conference video.

options.error_type: Confuses video input with audio input
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An audio analyzer is intended for audio input, while the input here is recorded video.
options.better_fit: Use an audio analyzer for a call recording or another audio file.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead would choose an analyzer that does not match the conference video.
feedback.instructional: Match the analyzer to the input type: recorded video uses prebuilt-videoSearch.

options.error_type: Confuses meeting video with invoice documents
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An invoice analyzer extracts invoice-oriented fields, not meeting details from a video conference.
options.better_fit: Use an invoice analyzer for invoices containing billing fields such as tax and total.

feedback.intrinsic: The requested meeting details would be replaced by invoice-oriented fields.
feedback.instructional: Choose prebuilt-videoSearch for recorded video conferences.

exercises.explanation: Correct—the video analyzer is the appropriate decision for video input and structured meeting details.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The counts would be difficult to interpret.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the image result, then state the in-person count, remote count, and total.

exercises.correct_answer: The image returned one in-person attendee three remote attendees and four total.
exercises.explanation: The result identifies the image report, then gives the in-person count, remote count, and total. This order makes the attendance breakdown clear.

exercises.question_text: What format makes media analysis results predictable for later systems?

options.rationale: This is correct. Predictable JSON results make extracted information easier for later systems to use.

options.error_type: Confuses structured results with input content
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A scanned page image is source content, not a predictable structured result format.
options.better_fit: Use this as input when analyzing a document or image.

feedback.intrinsic: Later work would still require extracting the information from the image.
feedback.instructional: JSON results organize extracted fields for later use.

options.error_type: Confuses source media with analysis output
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An unprocessed recording is source media and has not been transformed into structured results.
options.better_fit: Use this as input for audio or video analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting details would remain locked in the recording.
feedback.instructional: Analysis produces structured JSON results from the recording.

options.error_type: Confuses structured output with manual processing
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A paper note is not a predictable structured format for system use.
options.better_fit: Use this for an informal human reminder, not for structured extracted results.

feedback.intrinsic: Searching and automating meeting details would be harder.
feedback.instructional: JSON supports storage, search, and automation.

exercises.explanation: Correct—predictable JSON results are easier for later systems to use.

exercises.question_text: Which fields can capture changes during a video meeting? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Time intervals show attendance as it changes during the recording.
This is correct. A video schema can include details of who spoke.
This is correct. A video schema can include what each speaker said.

options.error_type: Confuses video-over-time fields with an image field
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A still-image location describes one camera image and does not capture activity over a recording.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing a single conference-room camera image.

feedback.intrinsic: Changes in attendance and speaking would be missed.
feedback.instructional: Video fields can follow attendance and speakers over time.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these fields can capture changing meeting activity.

exercises.question_text: Predictable ___ results make later business processes easier.

parts.text: results make later business processes easier.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The extracted details would be less ready for automation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use JSON for the structured result format; OCR, transcripts, and schemas serve different roles.

exercises.explanation: JSON is a structured text format for storing and exchanging data. Predictable JSON results make extracted fields easier to use in later processes.

exercises.question_text: Order the pieces to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The speaker field would be described unclearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the schema, then state that it can record who spoke during the meeting.

exercises.correct_answer: A video schema can record who spoke during the meeting.
exercises.explanation: A video schema can record who spoke during the meeting, illustrating that video analysis can capture speaker information.

exercises.question_text: Which information can video analysis unlock? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Video and meeting-image analysis can identify a meeting location.
This is correct. A video meeting schema can include who spoke.
This is correct. A video recording schema can include a discussion summary.
This is incorrect. OCR produces editable printed text, while video analysis can provide broader meeting information.
options.better_fit: Use this for OCR on a scanned document or receipt.

feedback.intrinsic: Important speaker and action details would be left out.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads printed text; video analysis extracts meeting insights.

exercises.explanation: Correct—video analysis can extract location, speakers, and a discussion summary.
